source_text: Cui infusum est oleum chrismatis. Unctio Spiritus. Christiani a Christo.
thought_title: The Anointing of Christ and Christians
orientation: Origen is describing the greatness of Christ as the great priest, and now explains how the anointing oil was poured into him and how Christians receive their name from Christ.
pass_a_gloss: To whom the oil of chrism has been poured in. The anointing of the Spirit. Christians from Christ.

choices.english: To whom the oil of chrism has been poured in
choices.why: Keeps the dative of recipient and the passive perfect of infundo to show the completed action of anointing upon Christ
rejected: Into whom the chrism oil was poured
Who has had the oil of chrism poured into him

choices.why: Renders the noun phrase as a bare appositional statement, preserving the terse explanatory force of the Latin
Keeps the preposition a with the ablative to show derivation or source, matching the Latin's compact etymological point
rejected: Christians take their name from Christ

pass_b_english: Into him the oil of chrism has been poured. The anointing of the Spirit. Christians from Christ.

last_rejected.why: "Cui" is dative/ablative, but context shows this refers back to the high priest (pontifex) previously mentioned. "Into him" is wrong preposition and awkward; "Upon whom" or "To whom" would convey the anointing sense correctly.
last_rejected.fix: Upon whom the oil of chrism has been poured.
last_rejected.ruling: Cui is dative/ablative; 'into him' is a reasonable rendering for oil poured on someone. Preference for 'upon whom' is not a major error.
